summary: Inserts a key/value string pair (a2, a3) into a growable string table stored at this (this[0] = capacity, this[1] = count, this[2] = entries pointer). Rejects the pair with -1 when a2 is null, a3 is null, either string is empty, or the two strings are equal. When count has reached capacity the table grows by 128 slots: a new buffer of 16 * new_capacity + 4 bytes is allocated (4-byte header holding the new capacity, followed by entries initialized to {0, -1, 0, -1}), each existing entry's two string fields are duplicated through StringCopyWithBufferRealloc (null strings substituted with byte_5EA438), and the old buffer's entry strings and header are freed. The count is then incremented and both new strings are duplicated via StringCopyWithBufferRealloc before returning 0. Called by sub_423890 (0x00423890).

operations.description: Early-out: if the key a2 is null, return -1.
Early-out: if a3 is null, strlen(a2) is zero, strlen(a3) is zero, or strcmp(a2, a3) is zero (equal strings), return -1.
Growth branch taken when the count this[1] (offset 0x4) is >= the capacity this[0] (offset 0x0).
Grows capacity: v6 = this[0] + 128 and this[0] = v6.
OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper(16 * (v5 + 128) + 4) allocates the new buffer: 4 bytes of header plus 16 bytes per entry.
When allocation succeeds the header word is set to the new capacity v6 and the entry region begins at v7 + 1; on failure the new entries pointer v20 is set to 0.
Initializes each of the new-capacity entries to {0, -1, 0, -1} (4 dwords per entry).

Copy pass over the existing count this[1] entries (16-byte stride from this[2]): each entry's two string fields (+0 and +8) are read, substituted with &byte_5EA438 when null, and each passed to StringCopyWithBufferRealloc.
Frees the old buffer: walks its entries backwards freeing each entry's two string pointers via ShortComputation_4370, then FreeWrapper_7bcf frees the buffer header at this[2] - 4.
Repoints this[2] (offset 0x8) at the new entries buffer v20.
Duplicates the new key a2 and the new value a3 through StringCopyWithBufferRealloc (the duplicated pointers are stored into the entry region on the caller's behalf via the buffer writes).
Returns 0 on success; all rejection paths return -1.

clean_pseudocode: if (v7) { v7[0] = this[0]; v20 = v7 + 1; init each entry to {0,-1,0,-1}; }
if (this[2]) { for each old entry: ShortComputation_4370(s1); ShortComputation_4370(s0); FreeWrapper_7bcf(this[2] - 4); }
